newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Soccer-Venables divides opinion in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Soccer-Venables divides opinion in Australia.

text.p: The likely appointment of Terry Venables as Australia's national team coach prompted a backlash of criticism on Monday in what could be his new soccer home.
But the former England and Barcelona coach received support from the man he is expected to replace, departing Australia coach Eddie Thomson.
Venables, who quit as England coach after guiding them to the semifinals of Euro 96, was quoted in the British media on Sunday as saying he was now "99 percent in position" to accept the job.
Former Australia goalkeeper Jack Reilly on Monday described the situation as a disgrace and a "slap in the face" for all those involved in the local game.

"This is totally inconceivable, an absolute farce. He (Venables) knows nothing about Australian conditions...and knows little or nothing about our overseas and local players," Reilly told Monday's The Australian newspaper.
Former Australia defender David Ratcliffe joined the chorus of disapproval, questioning Venables' coaching record.
"There are Dutch, Germans and South Americans who have just as good, if not better, credentials than Venables," said Ratcliffe, coach of Sydney UTS Olympic in the domestic national league.
But Thomson, who resigned last month after six years in charge to join Hiroshima in the Japanese J-League, praised governing body Soccer Australia for targeting Venables.
"Terry is a great guy and will do wonders for the game. I'm positive he will get us to the World Cup (in France in 1998)," Thomson said.
He said Venables had contacted him on Saturday to seek his opinion and information about Australian players.

Australian media reported last week that Venables could be appointed under a novel job-sharing scheme that would allow him to spend most of his time in Europe and monitor the form of Australian players there in the lead-up to World Cup finals.
Thomson said such an arrangement made sense because more than 100 Australian players, including Aston Villa goalkeeper Mark Bosnich and Lazio sweeper Paul Okon, are based overseas.
"If you had asked me three years ago, I would have said such a move was silly, but I believe the time is now ripe," Thomson said.
